name: Datasheet Snippet Extractor
blurb: pinout and absolute maximum tables from a PDF into structured data
intro: Reads the Absolute Maximum Ratings table and the pin table out of a datasheet's text, as pdftotext -layout writes it, into rows with min/max/unit and pin/name/type/description. In the app, choose the PDF and it is converted offline; it is a layout heuristic, so every row keeps its line number to check against the PDF.

inputs.label: Datasheet text (pdftotext -layout)

inputs.help: Columns must keep their spacing. In the app, the PDF picker above fills this; elsewhere run pdftotext -layout file.pdf - and paste the pages with the tables.

usage: Pass `text` as the datasheet's text from `pdftotext -layout` (only the pages with the tables is best), `part` as its name and `what` as both, absmax or pins. It returns the absolute maximum rows {parameter, condition, min, max, unit} (numbers where the cell is a number, else the text such as 'VIN + 0.3' or 'Internally limited') and the pins {pin, name, type, description}, as tables, JSON and CSV, with the source line of each row and the lines inside the tables it could not read. Check the rows against the PDF; for design limits use the recommended operating conditions, not these.
sources: Poppler pdftotext -layout (keeps the column layout as spaces)
Table reading: layout heuristic (header column positions, 2+ space cell breaks); JEDEC JEP184-style absolute maximum ratings semantics: stress limits, not operating conditions
